knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Radical Function Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=7x+1.$ Then $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}={u}^{-1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=7.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}\cdot (7) \\  & =-\frac{7}{2\sqrt{(7x+1{)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
